newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-MATTHAEUS WARNS BAYERN AGAINST COMPLACENCY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MATTHAEUS WARNS BAYERN AGAINST COMPLACENCY.

text.p: Bayern Munich captain Lothar Matthaeus has warned his team against complacency as the German league leaders prepare to take on one of the most unglamorous teams in the country on Saturday -- Duisburg.
The promoted team from a small town in the middle of the industrial Ruhr region have achieved little to shout about in the top echelons of the German game in the last 10 years.
Duisburg have spent more time since 1986 in the regional leagues and the second division than in the Bundesliga.

Although the 12th-placed team are not in the relegation zone at the moment, Bayern's array of highly-paid internationals should be capable to taking three points at home against a team of little-known players.
But former World Cup-winning captain Matthaeus said: "We don't need to motivate ourselves against teams like Borussia Dortmund, VfB Stuttgart and Bayer Leverkusen but we do against a team like this.
"It's a matter of showing character. At the end of the day it was against teams like this that we lost the championship last season."
Bayern, who have the best home record in the Bundesliga, have a three-point lead over reigning champions Borussia Dortmund after 19 games.
The Bavarians know they have a superb chance this weekend to stretch their lead over Dortmund whose eyes are starting to turn towards next week's European Cup quarter-finals.
Dortmund, who lost 2-0 at lowly Fortuna Duesseldorf last week, play hosts to 1860 Munich on Saturday.
Bayern are expected to be without their Euro 96 midfielder Mehmet Scholl who has pulled a calf muscle. Either Christian Nerlinger or Marcel Witeczek will replace Scholl.
Italian coach Giovanni Trapattoni must decide whether to bring international defender Thomas Helmer into the squad after a virus.
Despite the lack of attraction in the encounters, this could be a crucial weekend for the championship.
Dortmund must beat 1860 if they are to keep up their challenge following last week's disappointing defeat. Injuries and suspensions are not helping coach Ottmar Hitzfeld.
German international Joerg Heinrich is suspended for the game and Dortmund will also be without swift wing back Stefan Reuter who has a rib injury.
